questions.script:
M: Good afternoon. I’m James, the leader of our school band, Rockstars.
For the school festival next month, all of our band members are
practicing hard to put on a fantastic show. However, we want to
have a concert that everyone can enjoy. So, we’re asking you to
recommend some specific songs you want to hear us play. If you
have any songs in mind, please write them down on a piece of
paper. Then, drop it into the request box in front of the music room
by this Friday. We will select a few songs and perform them. Thank
you for your participation.

questions.script:
W: Leo, is something wrong with your legs?
M: Yes. I have a little pain in them. Maybe I exercised too much
yesterday.
W: Oh, did you stretch after exercising?
M: No. I was tired, so I just rested afterwards.
W: You shouldn’t skip stretching right after a workout.
M: Is it that important?
W: Yes. Without stretching, your muscles stay tight, and they hurt.
M: Oh, I didn’t know that.
W: Try spending just a few minutes stretching next time. It helps your
muscles recover faster.
M: That sounds helpful.
W: Yeah. Stretching after exercise can really reduce pain.
M: Okay. I’ll make sure to do it from now on.

questions.script:
W: Hello, viewers! Thanks for tuning in to my video channel,
All4HighSchool. When I first started high school, I hardly talked to
anyone and kept waiting for others to speak first. But I soon learned
something important: be the one who says hello first! A simple “Hi”
in the hallway can sometimes turn into a short, friendly chat. It can
make things easier around new people. Saying “Good morning” to
friends first can help build good relationships with them. So as you
begin this new school life, remember: a small greeting can be the
spark that builds new connections.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.

M: Hi, Emma. What are you looking at?
W: Hi. My friend took a picture of me on Sports Day. Look at this.
M: Oh, I see the Blue Team banner between two poles. Were you on
the Blue Team?
W: Yes. Our team did great this year.
M: Is that your cap, the one on the chair?
W: No, it’s not mine. I think someone left it there.
M: I see. You said you were volunteering after the games, right?
W: Yes. When this picture was taken, I was picking up a can that was
on the ground.
M: That’s nice. I like the striped shirt you were wearing.
W: Thanks. All the volunteers wore the same striped shirts.
M: Oh, I also see three soccer balls beside the pole.
W: Yes. Those were the balls used for the soccer game. I also had to
pick them up.
M: Wow, that sounds like a busy day. Thanks for sharing the picture
with me!

W: Hey, Jack, are you ready for the online group discussion?
M: Yes. But, I’m a little worried since it’s my first time hosting an
online discussion!
W: Really? Then, I can help you double check things before you start.
M: Thanks.
W: Did you share the online link in the group chat?
M: Yes, I did. I also uploaded the materials to the shared folder.
W: Nice. Have you checked the camera angle?
M: Yes, it’s all set.
W: You’re doing pretty good so far. [Pause] Oh, don’t forget to check
the microphone.
M: Don’t worry. I’ve already tested it. It works well.
W: Perfect. Okay, everything seems ready. You can start now.
M: Wait, I haven’t started the recording yet. I’ll start the recording
soon. Thank you for your help.
W: My pleasure. Good luck!

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
questions.script:
M: How may I help you?
W: Hi. I’m looking for some pajamas.
M: How about these? They’re our new cotton pajamas for spring.
W: Let me see. Oh, I like the pattern. They look comfortable. How
much are they?
M: They are 20 dollars.
W: Oh, sounds good. What sizes do you have?
M: We have three sizes, small, medium, and large.
W: I’d like two pairs of pajamas, both medium size, please. One for me
and one for my mom.
M: That’s sweet! Your mother will love them. Do you also want these
socks to go with them? They are 5 dollars for each pair.
W: Yes, I’ll take two pairs.
M: Perfect. So, you need two pairs of pajamas and two pairs of socks.
Is that correct?
W: Yes, that’s right. Can I use this coupon?
M: Sure. You can get 10 percent off of the total price.
W: Okay. Here’s my credit card.

M: Race Against Hunger? What’s that? What is it for?
W: It’s for promoting the importance of food for the next generation.
M: Sounds interesting. When will it take place?
W: It’ll be held from April 11th to April 29th.
M: Okay. What do participants do in the event?
W: They record their running or walking distance, and share it on their
social media.
M: I see. Is there any prize for the participants?
W: Yeah. If they meet the requirements, they’ll get a water bottle.

W: You can scan this QR code and fill out the application form online.
M: Great. Thanks.

M: Hello, students! This is Mike, your computer teacher. The AI
Coding Afterschool Program is coming up soon. This afterschool
program is for first graders who want to learn basic AI coding
skills. It will be held on Friday, May 8th, at the school computer
lab. It will last for three hours, starting at 4 p.m. and ending at 7

questions.script:
M: Jessie, I heard your sister’s birthday is next week. Do you have any
plans?
W: Yeah, we’re thinking about taking a one­day class together. I’ve
been looking at a few options.
M: Maybe I can help you choose. What kind of classes are you
interested in?
W: Umm... I want to try baking, so I’m trying to choose between Cake
Baking and Cookie Baking.
M: Then let’s narrow it down. What level are you looking for?
W: Since it’ll be our first class together, I’ll leave out the advanced
level.
M: Okay. You probably don’t want a big class, right?
W: Yes. I’d prefer a small group ― fewer than eight people.
M: Got it. Then you have two options left. How about the price?
W: It’s her birthday, so I’ll choose the more expensive one.
M: Then this class looks perfect for you.
W: Yeah, I think she’ll really enjoy it. I’ll book it right away!

M: Hello, listeners. Welcome to the Morning Fitness Guide. Do you
want to exercise more effectively in the morning? Eating food
before exercise can raise your energy level. So today, I’d like to
share some foods that are good to eat before a workout. First,
bananas are a popular choice because they provide quick energy and
help you feel less tired. Next, yogurt is light on the stomach and
gives your body some protein. Eggs are also a good option because
they keep you full for longer and improve your strength. Finally, a
small amount of nuts can help maintain your energy throughout
exercise. Trying these foods before exercise can lead to better
results. I hope these tips help you exercise effectively in the
morning.
